sourcedFrom: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. (2025)
cleanIntro: A 9mm compact pistol built on 1911 lines: a thumb safety on the left of the frame, a bull barrel with a flat-wire recoil spring on a guide rod carrying a Shok-Buff, a backstrap that swings away when the hammer spring housing is pressed in from the bottom of the frame, and grip panels held on by grip screws. Wilson Combat's schedule is round-counted: a quick clean every 300 rounds, the muzzle and compensator area every 200 to 300, a thorough clean and Shok-Buff check every 1,200, and the extractor, firing pin and trigger group every 6,000. ⛔ The thumb safety must be DOWN before the slide will move, and the slide is eased down on an empty chamber, never slammed.

steps.title: Magazine out before anything else
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine release on the left of the frame, take the magazine out of the grip and set it aside, away from the pistol.
steps.prose: Magazine first, slide second. Run the slide with a loaded magazine still in and you have just chambered a round.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and set it aside.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 2, p.43

steps.title: Thumb safety down, then lock the slide back
steps.action: Push the thumb safety at the left rear of the frame down to FIRE. Then pull the slide fully back to extract and eject anything in the chamber, and lock it back on the slide stop.
steps.prose: With the safety up on SAFE the slide is blocked and will not move — that is the safety working, not a jam. Do not force the slide against it.
steps.quote: The slide will not retract, and you will not be able to load the handgun if the safety is in the SAFE (up)(a) position.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Loading the Chamber and Activating the Safety, p.32

steps.title: Look and feel: chamber empty, magazine out
steps.action: With the slide locked back, look into the chamber and the magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber. Both checks, every time.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat asks for the check to be visual and physical. A dark chamber can hide a cartridge from the eye; it cannot hide it from a finger.
steps.quote: Visually and physically confirm there is not a cartridge in the chamber, and the magazine is not in the handgun.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Unloading, step 3, p.35

steps.title: Eye protection on, 1/8-inch punch to hand
steps.action: Put on safety glasses before you start, and have the takedown tool that came with the pistol, or a 1/8-inch steel punch, on the bench — the backstrap step needs it.
steps.prose: The recoil spring and the hammer spring housing are both under compression in this strip, and a spring that gets away goes for your face.
steps.quote: Wear adequate eye protection when disassembling this or any firearm.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 1, p.43

steps.title: Align the takedown notch, push the slide stop out
steps.action: Ease the slide forward from lock-back and draw it back just until the takedown notch in the slide lines up with the inner lug of the slide stop. Then push the slide stop all the way out from the right and take it off the frame.
steps.prose: Line the notch up first. A slide stop pushed out against a misaligned slide drags across the frame and scratches an arc beside its hole.
steps.quote: Retract the slide to align the take down notch of the slide with the inner lug of the slide stop, completely push the slide stop out and remove.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 3, p.44

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, fingers cupped over the spring
steps.action: Run the slide assembly forward off the front of the frame with your fingers cupped under it, so the recoil spring and guide rod cannot jump out as the slide clears.
steps.prose: The spring is still under tension when the slide comes free. Cupped fingers keep the spring, its guide rod and the Shok-Buff on the rod from launching.
steps.quote: Slide the assembly forward to remove from the frame, while capturing the recoil spring and guide with your fingers cupped.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 4, p.45

steps.title: Ease the spring off, guide rod out, then the plug
steps.action: Let the flat-wire recoil spring relax under control, then lift the recoil spring and guide rod out of the slide, keeping the Shok-Buff on the base of the rod. Then take the recoil spring plug out of the front of the slide.
steps.prose: Ease it, do not let it go: the spring still carries load as it comes free. Keep the spring, rod and buffer together so they go back the way they came out.
steps.aside: 6. Remove the recoil spring plug from the slide.
steps.quote: Carefully ease the recoil spring to relax it’s tension, then remove the recoil spring and guide from the slide assembly.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 5, p.46

steps.title: Link forward and down, barrel out
steps.action: Swing the barrel link forward until it folds down against the underside of the chamber, then draw the bull barrel out of the slide.
steps.prose: With the link folded flat the barrel passes out freely. If it hangs up, the link has not folded all the way.
steps.quote: Pivot the barrel link forward and down against the underside of the barrel chamber and pull the barrel out of the slide.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 7, p.47

steps.title: Hammer down carefully onto its rest
steps.action: On the frame, lower the hammer under control so it rests against the front of the hammer slot. Do not let it fall freely.
steps.prose: ⛔ Wilson Combat warns that skipping this can damage the pistol: the backstrap that comes off next holds the hammer spring housing, and it is released with the hammer at rest.
steps.quote: Lower the hammer carefully, so it is at rest with the front of the hammer slot in the frame.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 8, p.48
steps.warn: Failure to do so can damage your firearm.

steps.title: Takedown tool in, backstrap swings away
steps.action: Put the takedown tool into the hole at the bottom of the frame and compress the hammer spring housing, while pressing upward on the bottom of the backstrap's beavertail. When the backstrap swings freely, pivot it away from the grip.
steps.prose: Both pressures at once — the tool compressing the housing and your thumb lifting the beavertail. With only one, the backstrap stays put.
steps.quote: Insert the included takedown tool in the hole at the bottom of the frame, compress the hammer spring housing at the same time, while placing upward pressure on the bottom of the backstrap beavertail.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 9, p.49

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is the strip as Wilson Combat writes it for the EDC X9 2.0: slide, bull barrel, recoil spring and guide rod with the Shok-Buff, the recoil spring plug, the slide stop, and the backstrap swung away. The grip panels stay on — they are held by grip screws and are not part of this strip. Look every part over for abnormal wear or breakage now.
steps.prose: Any part showing damage, unusual wear or breakage means the pistol is not used until Wilson Combat has been contacted. The firing pin, the extractor and the trigger group are a round-count job, in Deep Clean.
steps.aside: Inspect all parts for abnormal wear and breakage at this time.
steps.quote: You now have the frame disassembled as needed for normal cleaning and lubrication.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 10, p.50

steps.title: The bore: slow, full-length strokes with a nylon brush
steps.action: Put a 9mm nylon bore brush on a cleaning rod, wet it with bore cleaner, and run it through the bore several times, pushing all the way through on every stroke. Let it stand 3 to 5 minutes, spray degreaser through and let it dry, then run patches on a slotted tip until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Full-length strokes, not short scrubbing — reversing a brush halfway down the bore is hard on the brush and the rod.
steps.aside: Allow to stand for 3 to 5 minutes then wipe clean with a dry patch.
steps.quote: When cleaning the bore, use slow complete strokes (full length of bore) with a properly sized nylon brush.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

steps.title: Muzzle and compensator area, every 200 to 300 rounds
steps.action: Clean the carbon off the muzzle end of the barrel and the compensator area. Wilson Combat allows this one with the pistol fully assembled and the slide locked open, so it can be done between full cleanings.
steps.prose: How often depends on how clean the ammunition burns — dirtier loads, shorter interval.
steps.aside: This maintenance can be performed with the firearm fully assembled by locking the slide in the open position.
steps.quote: Inspect and clean the muzzle and compensator area of the barrel to minimize carbon buildup and maintain optimal performance.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Recommended Maintenance, Every 200-300 rounds, p.64

steps.title: Wipe away dirt and fouling, inside and out
steps.action: Wipe the slide and frame rails, the breech face, the barrel exterior and the chamber with non-abrasive patches or swabs. Where the inside of the pistol is caked with carbon, apply a carbon remover or bore cleaner first and let it work.
steps.prose: Non-abrasive is the word that matters on a finished pistol: nothing that scratches the rails or the finish.
steps.quote: Wipe away dirt and fouling on the interior and exterior of the firearm with non-abrasive patches or swabs.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

steps.title: Shok-Buff off the guide rod and inspected, every clean
steps.action: Take the Shok-Buff off the base of the guide rod, look at both sides, and replace it if it is cut, torn or swollen. Wipe the guide rod with a clean patch. Refit it with the groove at the top of the Shok-Buff aligned with the base of the guide rod, before the recoil spring goes back on.
steps.prose: ⚠ At the minimum the buffer is replaced every 1,200 rounds whatever it looks like. Wilson Combat recommends it for general use; it is not required for safe and reliable operation.
steps.quote: At the minimum, replace the buffer every 1200 rounds.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Inspecting The Shok-Buff, p.67

steps.title: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces and the rails
steps.action: After cleaning, put a light film of oil on the moving parts — the barrel locking surfaces and lugs, the barrel hood, and the frame and slide rails. Light, not heavy.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat picks the oil by temperature: the regular oil at 60 degrees or warmer, the light oil below that.
steps.quote: Make sure to lubricate the barrel locking surfaces and frame/slide rails.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Glasses on, rear of the slide pointed somewhere safe
deepSteps.action: Every 6,000 rounds Wilson Combat has the firing pin out to clean its channel and fit a new firing pin spring. Put on safety glasses and point the rear of the slide away from yourself and anyone else before you touch the firing pin stop.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The firing pin and its spring are under compression and can leave the slide hard — the book says it will shoot out as in a 1911.
deepSteps.quote: Before removing the firing pin and stop, make sure that the rear of the slide is pointed in a safe direction.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66
deepSteps.warn: Modern firearms contain springs that are under compression and can eject with significant striking force causing eye or other bodily injury.

deepSteps.title: Punch the firing pin in, stop down and out
deepSteps.action: Hold the rear of the slide firmly and press the firing pin in with a 1/8-inch punch to take the spring pressure off the stop. Keep a finger on the firing pin while you slide the stop down and out of the way, so the pin cannot eject.
deepSteps.prose: Your finger on the pin is what keeps it in the slide. Take it away before the stop is clear and the pin goes.
deepSteps.quote: Use your finger to retain the firing pin while sliding the stop down and out of the way.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66

deepSteps.title: Let the spring out slowly, then spring off the pin
deepSteps.action: Let the firing pin spring release its compression slowly, then take the pin and spring out of the slide. Separate them by turning the firing pin clockwise while pulling the spring firmly off. Clean the firing pin channel, and fit a new firing pin spring when it goes back in — the old one is discarded.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin spring is part of the drop safety: Wilson Combat has it replaced every 5,000 rounds of live fire or 5,000 dry fires.
deepSteps.aside: Slowly allow the firing pin spring to release its compressed spring tension and then remove it from the slide.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin spring from the firing pin by turning the firing pin clockwise and firmly pulling off the spring.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin: heat first, then out with the hex wrench
deepSteps.action: With the slide off and the recoil spring assembly and barrel set aside, heat the bottom of the extractor pin area of the slide with a torch or soldering iron to break the threadlocker, then turn the threaded pin counterclockwise with the supplied .050-inch hex wrench, holding the extractor with your hand as the pin comes out.
deepSteps.prose: Heat is needed the first time because the pin is set in threadlocker. Keep a hand on the extractor as the pin clears its pocket.
deepSteps.quote: Retain the extractor with your hand while removing the pin.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Extractor Removal/Cleaning, p.69

deepSteps.title: Extractor and pocket clean, dry underneath
deepSteps.action: Clean the carbon off the extractor and out of the extractor pocket thoroughly. Replace the extractor spring now. Leave no excess oil under the extractor when it goes back, then reassemble in reverse order and test it with a dummy round under the hook.
deepSteps.prose: Oil pooled under the extractor collects carbon and stops it closing on the case rim — exactly the failure to extract this job is meant to cure.
deepSteps.aside: Test your extractor by placing a dummy round under your extractor hook.
deepSteps.quote: Do not leave excessive oil or lubricant under the extractor pocket when reassembling.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Extractor Removal/Cleaning, p.69

deepSteps.title: Grip screws out, grip panels off
deepSteps.action: For the trigger group the grips come off. Thumb safety down to the firing position and the hammer lowered gently, then take out the grip screws with a screwdriver that fits them properly and lift the grip panels off the frame.
deepSteps.prose: A screwdriver that fits the slot is the point: a loose bit strips the screw heads or the threads in the frame bushings.
deepSteps.aside: Once the screws are removed, lift the grip panels off the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Use the appropriate screwdriver to carefully unscrew and remove the grip screws, taking care not to strip the screws or damage the threads.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Replacing Grips & Backstrap, p.68

deepSteps.title: Trigger group: aerosol cleaner, then sparing oil
deepSteps.action: With the grip panels off, spray the trigger group components with an aerosol cleaner made for firearms, let it dry, and put a sparing amount of oil on the exposed parts of the trigger group.
deepSteps.prose: Sparingly is the instruction. The book directs cleaning these parts in place, not taking them out.
deepSteps.quote: Remove grips, clean trigger group components with aerosol cleaner designed for firearms use and re-lubricate exposed parts of trigger group sparingly
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Recommended Maintenance, Every 6000 rounds, p.64

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: 9mm nylon brush with bore cleaner, full-length strokes from end to end
Stand 3 to 5 minutes, degreaser through, then patches until clean

cleaning.name: MUZZLE
tasks: Muzzle and compensator area cleaned of carbon
Every 200 to 300 rounds — can be done assembled, slide locked open

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and the inside of the slide wiped with non-abrasive patches
Carbon remover on anything caked, then wiped

cleaning.name: SHOK-BUFF
tasks: Off the guide rod, both sides inspected
Replaced if cut, torn or swollen — and every 1,200 rounds regardless
Refitted with its groove aligned to the base of the guide rod

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces, lugs and hood
Light oil on the frame and slide rails

reassembly: Backstrap pivoted back into place against the grip, over the hammer spring housing.
Barrel back into the slide with the link folded forward and down; recoil spring plug back in.
Shok-Buff on the base of the guide rod with its groove aligned, then the recoil spring and guide rod back into the slide assembly.
Slide assembly back onto the frame from the front, the takedown notch aligned with the slide stop, and the slide stop pushed back in.
Wilson Combat's instruction is to reverse the disassembly steps; ease the slide forward on the empty pistol — never let it slam.
fncheck: Unloaded and proven, magazine out, muzzle in a safe direction — Wilson Combat asks for this test after every disassembly and reassembly. Thumb safety: cock the hammer, push the safety up to SAFE and press the trigger — the safety stays on and the hammer does not move. Disconnector: with the hammer cocked, draw the slide back ¼ to ½ inch and press the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Half-cock: set the hammer on half-cock and press the trigger with a full grip — the hammer must not move. If the hammer falls or moves in any of these, or you see it follow to half-cock when the slide closes, do not use the pistol and contact Wilson Combat.
